title: Making a Mega Man X-inspired Metroidvania. Here's some gameplay after 4 months of development
author: Cautious_Material_40
selftext:
Been working on this for about 4 months now, mostly using AI to help with the coding in Unity.

I'm doing a ton of hands-on playtesting though, constantly tweaking movement, combat, enemy behavior, level layouts, etc.

Recently ripped a bunch of enemies from the Mega Man X games to use as placeholders and have been implementing my own AI and attack patterns for them. Also been working on mini-bosses with different mechanics, trying to make the encounters a little more interesting than just shooting everything until it dies.

I'm using a mix of purchased assets and placeholders right now, and working with a pixel artist on custom animations and additional artwork.

Level design has probably been my biggest struggle so far. I'm going for a mix of Mega Man X and Metroidvania-style exploration, and finding that balance between keeping things moving and giving players reasons to explore has been tricky.

That said, things have been feeling better and better with each round of changes. It's been a LOT of trial and error, and I've sunk way more hours into this than I originally expected.

Anyway, figured I'd share some gameplay and get some outside opinions since I've been staring at this thing for months.

Would love some feedback on the combat, movement, enemy encounters, or level design. Anything look particularly fun, boring, awkward, or just plain bad?

Don't worry about hurting my feelings. I've already hurt them plenty trying to design these levels.

comments.author: Cautious_Material_40
comments.body:
So for the level design, I essentially had ai build out the 30+ some rooms in a metroidvania style map for me.
It built the areas with no scenery or decoration, just basic blocks and areas. 
Im going back in to each room and redoing them entirely and adding the scenery elements to make it feel and look good.
AI is absolutely terrible at making levels that are fun, and does this know how to make an area look good ive found, so thats been a very manually intensive part of the process.
The spot with the boss really was just a hole in the ground, I hadn't really "updated", that section of the level yet, just wanted a spot for the mini boss encounter to happen.

Im curious, does the level design look okay? Does it look like an area you want to explore? 
What could I improve on the level design from what you have seen in this video?
